checked_scope: Common adverse sorting, threshold-mixture reduction, and exact zero-revenue optimum
checks: DSIC, IR and no subsidies give monotone x, U(0)=0 and U(r)=integral_0^r x. Equal-mass comparison with 1{r<a} and the sign of U-U(a) proves the same adverse sorting for every mechanism.

Threshold integration gives welfare W(a-t)_+^2/2 and payment t(1-t). The Stieltjes threshold mixture and harmless atomless endpoint changes yield a compact convex-hull problem; a supporting line gives at most two threshold contacts.

For zero revenue weight, convexity gives f(z)<=z*f(1), hence value<=qWa^2/2, attained by uniform free rationing. Deterministic unrationed prices require t>=1-q and can have zero welfare when q<=1-a, a<1; the result expressly excludes rationed-price mechanisms.
